name: 28-standing-desync-reported
description:
The mirror image of scenario 27, created BY HAND in the field the same morning: while unsticking cam-wohn-ofen the operator drove the board script to day while timps stood on night. Afterwards the two disagreed in the OTHER direction - decided mode night, ISP rendering Day - and nothing said so; the automaton would simply have flipped the ISP back at its next opportunity. Resolved only by a requested probe ({"daynight":{"probe":1}}), after which timps itself decided day (r=0.98) and the two agreed.

What must happen here is precisely NOT what happens in 27: no enforcement. A standing disagreement outside the readback-gate window may be a deliberate manual override, and forcing it back would clobber exactly the intervention the operator just made. So the requirement is a report: one WARN once the mismatch has stood DN_DESYNC_MS (20 s - well past any switch transient, and the gate window already covers the 18 s after a commanded switch), naming both sides and the resolution path (the requested probe), then silence; and one INFO when they agree again, so the episode has a visible end and the next episode can report anew.

The shape: a stable lit interior at night (illuminator carries it, boot verify is silent, r=4, zero clicks). At t=60 the override forces the served ISP mode to Day; the day pipeline deliberately reads the SAME 2000 as the night pipeline so no trigger fires and the desync STANDS - a scene where path C or the trend would fire would resolve itself and test nothing (that self-resolution is 27's and 16's business). At t=150 the operator undoes it; ISP back to Night, agreement, INFO. The budgets are the teeth: 0 board switches proves report-not-enforce (an enforcing build spends 2 clicks here and fails), and the forbid on the gate's own lines proves the notice did not fire THROUGH the gate. Pre-fix (gate only, no notice) this scenario fails all four expect_log assertions: the desync stood for 90 s and the log never mentioned it.

RESTATED 2026-08-22 (boot measures before it decides): the zero-switch budget became 2, because boot now measures with a real probe pair before the override window opens at t=60. The teeth are kept and sharpened rather than filed down: the forbids on 'switching to day'/'switching to night' are now negative lookaheads that exclude ONLY the boot measurement's own two drives, so an enforcing build still fails on the very first click it spends chasing the override - which is what this scenario is for.

expect_log: decided mode is night but the ISP has been rendering Day for \d+ s
not enforcing, this may be a manual override
decided mode and ISP agree again \(night\)
forbid_log: giving up until the next mode change
